name: jailbreaks
one_liner: A public collection of fake system prompts and persona tricks people paste into AI chatbots to try to get them to ignore their safety rules.
buyer: Honestly, there isn't a legitimate paying buyer here — the repo's own stated purpose is research into prompt-injection resistance, not a commercial product.
business_use_cases: A company's AI safety or security team references entries like these as test cases when red-teaming their own chatbot's defenses.
An AI vendor's trust-and-safety team studies the collection to understand current instruction-override techniques they need to guard against.
A security researcher writing about prompt-injection risk cites patterns from it as examples in a report for clients.

money_ideas.idea: An AI red-teaming consultant could reference entries like these while running a paid security assessment of a client's chatbot deployment.

steal_this: There's no real weekend business here. If you work in AI security, the one legitimate move is running your own chatbot against a few of these prompts to see if it holds up — not building anything that uses them to bypass a product's rules.
